blocks.value: There are two ways to create a thread: extend the Thread class and override run(), or implement the Runnable interface.

start() is what actually launches the thread. It calls run() on a separate line of execution and returns immediately without waiting for run() to finish, which is why "Outside of a thread" can print before or interleaved with the thread's own output.
Implementing Runnable instead keeps your class free to extend something else, since Java only allows single inheritance:
